content:
Facts: Creditor challenged deceased's 2019 holographic will revoking prior 2011 public will, claiming 2019 will null because not handwritten due to two witness-signatures at document-bottom; plaintiff alleged interest based on debt-acknowledgment claim against deceased; defendants contested lack of standing and argued witness-signatures separate from testamentary text not affecting validity.
Legal Framework: Articles 602, 606 Italian Civil Code (holographic autography requirement; nullity for form defects); case law on third-party intervention effects (Cass. 26258/2008).
Interpretive Issues: Whether witness signatures affixed at holographic will bottom after testator's completion constitute form-defect invalidating will; distinction between third-party intervention during drafting versus post-completion additions; scope of autography principle preventing same-document containing both valid holographic will and third-party writings; plaintiff-creditor standing to challenge will validity; effect of witness presence during drafting versus textual intervention.
Principles Applied: Plaintiff-creditor possesses standing challenging holographic will claiming debt against deceased; interest grounded in alleged credit relationship. Art. 602(1) handwriting-signature-date constitute essential validity requirements; presence necessary ensuring deceased-provision authenticity, complete document-authenticity excluding tampering/falsification, guaranteeing testator-wishes correspondence. Autography must concern every testamentary-transaction element, not only signature; last-will provisions written entirely by testator; formal-requirement absence renders will null per Art. 606(1) without effect. Autography principle per Art. 602 does not prevent same-document containing: (a) holographic will fully complying with law-requirements; (b) third-party writings affixed after testator's signature, placed in different part from testamentary-disposition area, incapable invalidating independently-drafted will. Holographic will nullity occurs only when text altered by third-party hand-insertion of even single word during last-will disposition-course. Present case: documented/undisputed that witness-signatories inserted no words into will written entirely/signed by testator. Witness-signatures affixed after will-drafting/testator-signing not themselves sufficient invalidating will with nullity-sanction. Plaintiff's fraud-allegation (witnesses inevitably present during drafting potentially invalidating contents) mentioned generally without specific substantiation/proof; fraud requires proving deception/trickery by witnesses swaying testator's will in otherwise-untaken direction. Will written/signed by testator himself; nullity-claim cannot succeed. Witness-presence during drafting (potentially influencing decisions) differs from textual-intervention; latter alone affects validity when occurring during disposition-drafting. Third-party writing-placement after testator-signature in different document-section preserves will-validity as independent testator-drafted instrument. ID: ITI106; Instance_Type: First instance; Legal_Duration: P9M; Law: IT – Civil Code – 602(1), 606(1); State: IT; Type: Succession; Costs: Heir 1 - 2906; Type_of_succession: Testamentary; law: Divorce
